# SHIBUSDT #89469 near-TP continuation investigation Г?" 2026-10-10

- Status: investigation approved; implementation is explicitly not approved.
  This workstream must not alter or delay FIX-153 release work.
- Hypothesis to test: a breached profit lock close to target may sometimes
  continue when current market structure and momentum remain supportive.
- Important counter-hypothesis: `1h=NEUTRAL` is not positive continuation
  evidence merely because 1m/5m are `WATCH`. Relaxing that guard on distance
  to TP alone could create false holds in weak or sideways markets.
- Required evidence before a policy change: use historical Replay/production
  evidence to compare the current exit rule against a hypothetical bounded
  hold using only information available at the breach. Segment results by
  1h/5m context, regime, trend structure, momentum, retracement depth and
  target-progress band. Evaluate TP hit rate, retained profit, adverse move,
  drawdown, and false-hold frequency. No post-exit price may inform entry or
  exit eligibility.
- Rejected approach: do not authorize continuation from `WATCH/WATCH/NEUTRAL`
  or near-TP distance alone.
- Code-review refinement: `PositionExitPolicy` creates a sharp tier boundary:
  with supportive 5m/current evidence, 1h `WATCH` can hold a breached lock but
  1h `NEUTRAL` falls through to `PROFIT_LOCK_EXIT`. Existing FIX-11T near-TP
  protection arms at 90% target progress and is evaluated after the ordinary
  lock-breach exit, so it could not affect #89469 at 84.28% progress.
- Fee-model refinement: `WalletAutoExecutionService` writes `fee_usdt=0` for
  paper BUY, SELL, and near-TP partial-harvest executions. Any policy Replay
  comparison must add an explicit fee/slippage model before claiming protected
  gross profit is a net gain.
- Approved experiment protocol from independent review: Production policy is
  unchanged. Compare (A) existing immediate lock exit, (B) a one-window,
  near-TP continuation using existing time-safe structure/momentum/context
  calculations, and (C) a volatility-adjusted tighter trailing exit. Use a
  pre-registered 85% TP-progress primary threshold; #89469 at 84.28% does not
  qualify and must not drive threshold selection. Require non-bearish 5m/1h,
  a fee-adjusted protected floor with modeled adverse fills, explicit numeric
  momentum/retracement definitions, no timer resets or repeated extensions,
  and strictly as-of-breach evidence. Evaluate net expectancy, drawdown,
  false-hold/adverse-move rate, and include later-decline counterexamples;
  reserve an out-of-sample period before any implementation decision.
- Final protocol controls: calculate TP progress only from immutable original
  entry and original TP; exclude and report zero/negative/invalid target
  distance. Every A/B/C candidate must use identical historical data,
  evaluation periods, and fee/slippage assumptions. Candidate B must model an
  intrawindow price path sufficiently to determine which of its emergency
  floor or target was reached first; candle high/low alone is not evidence of
  that order. Pre-register the minimum sample size, required net-expectancy
  improvement, and maximum allowed drawdown deterioration before results are
  viewed, then report the qualification count for the B cohort.
- Final cohort and comparison definition: Candidate B is eligible only in the
  85% to strictly-less-than-90% original-TP-progress band, with fresh,
  quality-valid 1h `NEUTRAL`, supportive fresh/quality-valid 5m, and required
  current-frame structure/momentum evidence. Missing, stale, invalid, or
  unknown 1h/5m evidence makes the case ineligible rather than non-bearish.
  This avoids changing or competing with existing FIX-11T behaviour at 90%.
  Pre-count the eligible cohort; insufficient sample means keep collecting.
  B-versus-A is the sole primary comparison; C is secondary/exploratory and
  must have its trailing formula fixed before Replay. Verify ATR, spread, and
  tick-size availability as of breach; if historical spread is unavailable,
  use a declared fixed assumption and sensitivity analysis.
- Final breach semantics: eligibility uses `breach_tp_progress`, calculated
  from the executable price at the exact profit-lock breach, not the historic
  high-water mark. Persist/report both `max_tp_progress` and
  `breach_tp_progress`. The continuation emergency floor is distinct from the
  breached original lock; if actual executable price (including modeled
  fee/spread/slippage) already violates that floor, exit immediately. Freeze
  numerical precision, 90%-boundary precedence (FIX-11T owns 90%+), hold
  length, tolerance, floor, costs, sample threshold, and success criteria
  before inspecting results. Report confidence intervals and chronological
  out-of-sample results; a small qualifying cohort is insufficient evidence.
- Team-2 final validity controls: create and commit a numerical pre-registration
  before any outcome is viewed, recording its immutable content hash here.
  Verify available intrabar path data; where tick/price-event evidence cannot
  order TP versus emergency-floor contact, mark the case ambiguous, apply one
  conservative adverse-move-first rule consistently, and report analyses both
  with and without those cases. Compute the floor per trade as
  `max(original_lock - tolerance, fee_adjusted_breakeven)` and report when
  breakeven binds. Compare A and B as paired outcomes on the same eligible
  breach events, reporting per-event B-minus-A and the count of later declines
  avoided by A.

# Replay-versus-Production parity audit Г?" 2026-10-10

- Scope: source-level comparison of the manual Regression/Replay pipeline with
  the current paper-trading Production path. No trading code, configuration,
  database data, or Replay result was changed.
- Confirmed shared authority: Replay regenerates technical indicators through
  `TechnicalIndicatorService`, signals through `AnalysisService`, BUY authority
  through `ExecutionIntelligenceService`, BUY/SELL validation through
  `TradeExecutionValidationService`, and normal exit, TP-continuation,
  profit-lock, and near-TP policies through the corresponding shared policy
  classes. When canonical `LEGACY`/`APPLIED` price events exist, the Replay
  consumes them in timestamp order before making the same close-candle signal
  visible, matching the documented live ordering.
- Confirmed boundary: Replay is a shadow simulation, not a transactionally
  identical copy of Production. It starts with fixed capital of 10,000 USDT,
  manages one symbol/position in isolation, uses replay-local daily budget and
  position state, and writes only `*_test` tables. It therefore cannot
  reproduce an actual wallet balance, simultaneous positions, global
  `maxOpenPositions`, daily loss limit, idempotency races, database locks, or
  real execution latency.
- Confirmed historical-evidence limitation: derivatives history is not
  persisted, so historical Replay always receives `UNAVAILABLE` derivatives
  context when that feature is enabled. Historical order-book evaluation uses
  stored snapshots only and becomes `UNAVAILABLE` when no snapshot exists,
  whereas live Production samples its in-memory/live Binance source. Such runs
  are useful simulations but are not full signal-parity proof unless the
  required historical evidence exists and is reported.
- Confirmed price-evidence limitation: a Replay run labels itself
  `EXACT_PRICE_REPLAY` whenever at least one accepted price event exists. It
  does not prove complete tick coverage for every time an open position needed
  protection. Windows with no accepted events fall back to signal prices and
  are labelled `SIGNAL_PRICE_FALLBACK`; neither fallback nor partial coverage
  should be described as tick-exact reproduction.
- Test evidence: Java 21 focused tests passed for profit-lock/TP-extension
  parity, position exit/continuation, near-TP policy, and shared sizing.
  Existing Replay-specific coverage is narrow: it does not execute a complete
  Production-versus-Replay scenario across entry, add, wallet controls,
  price-event ordering, partial harvest, and exit.
- Conclusion: Replay is suitable for controlled, manual strategy regression
  and the approved FIX-155 research work only when each run carries explicit
  evidence-quality labels. It is not yet valid to claim it is fully identical
  to Production in all phases. A future parity program must add deterministic
  scenario tests and a run-level eligibility contract before using Replay as a
  release-equivalence certificate.


--- TRADE INVESTIGATION AGENT ---
# Trade Investigation Agent

## Role

Investigate one Crypto AI Trader trade from durable evidence. Explain what
happened, why the system entered and exited, whether it followed the intended
rules, and whether the entry/exit was supported by the information available
at that time.

Investigations are read-only. Do not change code, configuration, services,
database records, review states, Replay work, or deployment state.

## Required input

Obtain or resolve:

- Environment and application: local, test, or production.
- Database host, port, and schema.
- One trade reference: `paper_position.id`, `wallet_trade.id`, or a symbol plus
  a bounded approximate entry-time window.
- Optional question or suspected issue.

Before analysis, confirm the symbol, trade/position ID, running version or FIX
level, and ingestion mode. Read the actual schema before choosing tables or
columns. Do not assume a table is in `crypto_ai` when it may belong to
`crypto_ai_v2`.

## Evidence rules

- Use configured database and SSH/log connections without displaying secrets.
- Use bounded, read-only queries and targeted log searches.
- Treat stored timestamps as UTC; display both UTC and KSA (`UTC+03:00`).
- Attach record IDs and timestamped log evidence to every factual conclusion.
- Distinguish **confirmed fact**, **supported inference**, and **missing or
  conflicting evidence**.
- Missing logs or records do not prove that no execution/effect occurred.
- A saved signal does not prove execution. A callback return does not prove a
  transaction committed. Under FIX-153, `market_price_event.APPLIED` proves a
  committed successful protection callback, but can be a no-op when there was
  no open position; find the position/trade mutation separately.
- Current configuration does not prove which settings were active at entry. If
  no configuration history exists, report that limitation.

## Investigation workflow

### 1. Resolve identity and environment

Link the trade reference to, where available:

- `paper_position`
- `wallet_trade`
- entry and exit `trade_signal`
- `signal_processing_work`
- wallet/position execution records

Record entry and exit times in UTC and KSA. Confirm whether the trader ran in
local-candle OFF mode or a legacy shared-market mode.

### 2. Collect a small evidence bundle

Start with exact IDs and a narrow time window. Expand only when the evidence
requires it. Collect:

| Evidence | Establishes |
| --- | --- |
| `paper_position` | lifecycle, entry/exit, stop, target, status |
| `wallet_trade` | executed quantity, prices, fees, linked signal |
| `trade_signal` | decision, strategy, scores, entry eligibility, reasons |
| `signal_processing_work` | claim, attempt, completion, expiry, uncertainty |
| `candle` / `technical_indicator` | market data and analysis inputs available then |
| `market_price_event` | intra-candle protection observations and outcomes |
| configuration/version evidence | applicable rules, when historically available |
| application and timing logs | analysis, execution, protection, exceptions, waits |

Avoid fetching large signal explanation fields until they are needed.

### 3. Reconstruct the timeline

Build a timeline, explicitly showing missing stages:

`candle closed Г+' signal saved Г+' work claimed Г+' locks acquired Г+' entry committed Г+' protection observations Г+' exit decision Г+' exit committed`

Measure separately:

- candle close to signal generation;
- signal generation to processing/entry;
- observation time to protection completion;
- exit-trigger evidence to recorded exit.

Correlate delays only with logs/events for the same symbol, position, signal,
or price-event identity. A nearby slow SQL query is not proof of causation.

### 4. Assess entry correctness and quality

Use only evidence that was available at entry. Check:

- signal mode, closed-candle identity, freshness, and data quality;
- final decision and entry-allowed result;
- BTC context, higher-timeframe, ATR, liquidity, risk/reward, sizing, and
  strategy gates that applied at that time;
- correct signal/position linkage and absence of duplicate/stale-retry entry;
- quantity, wallet balance, risk limits, fees, and fill/reference-price gap.

Return two separate conclusions:

- **Execution correctness:** followed or violated the implemented rules.
- **Entry quality:** supported, weak, or unverifiable from contemporaneous
  evidence.

Subsequent price movement may evaluate the outcome; it must never be presented
as information the entry decision had.

### 5. Reconstruct protection and stop-loss behavior

For FIX-153, inspect accepted `LEGACY`/`APPLIED` price events and retain
`PENDING`, `NON_CANONICAL`, and `PROTECTION_NOT_APPLIED` records as evidence
gaps or exclusions. Never substitute candle OHLC for absent intra-candle price
evidence.

For each relevant accepted observation:

1. Determine the then-active stop, target, trailing stop, and profit-lock state.
2. Find the first accepted observation that met an exit threshold.
3. Confirm that protection evaluated it and identify the resulting position or
   wallet execution record.
4. Explain delays, rejections, stale/out-of-order classification, exceptions,
   lock waits, or pool pressure.

Classify the exit path accurately: fixed stop-loss, trailing stop, profit-lock,
take-profit, signal-driven exit, manual exit, or unknown.

### 6. Assess exit correctness and quality

Compare the recorded exit reason, quantity, and price with trigger evidence.
Check threshold reach, accepted-observation identity, protection timing, and
the committed execution. Calculate maximum favourable/adverse movement during
the holding period separately from the contemporaneous exit assessment.

### 7. Reconcile financial results

Recalculate using execution records:

- bought/sold quantities and weighted entry/exit prices;
- gross P&L, fees, and net P&L;
- partial exits, remaining quantity, and realized versus unrealized values.

Flag discrepancies among wallet records, position records, and UI output.

### 8. Diagnose cause and use Replay carefully

Classify findings as one or more of:

- strategy decision;
- data freshness or coverage;
- analysis delay;
- execution failure;
- protection failure;
- database, lock, or connection-pool contention;
- accounting/UI discrepancy;
- insufficient evidence.

Run Replay only as a controlled comparison with equivalent candles, accepted
prices, strategy version, and settings. State every unavailable input or
material difference. Never claim parity by substituting candle OHLC for missing
price evidence or treating `PENDING` as accepted.

## Required final report

1. **Trade identity and environment** Г?" IDs, symbol, version/mode, scope.
2. **UTC/KSA timeline** Г?" evidence-backed sequence and latency breakdown.
3. **Entry** Г?" execution correctness and entry quality.
4. **Exit** Г?" execution correctness and exit quality.
5. **Stop-loss/profit-lock** Г?" worked, failed, or unverifiable, with evidence.
6. **P&L reconciliation** Г?" quantities, prices, fees, and discrepancies.
7. **Root cause and confidence** Г?" confirmed defect, valid loss, configuration
   issue, delay, or insufficient evidence.
8. **Evidence references** Г?" record IDs, query/log timestamps, code/config
   references.
9. **Missing evidence** Г?" exactly what prevents a stronger conclusion.
10. **Recommended correction and regression checks** Г?" only when justified.

A profitable trade can violate the rules, and a losing trade can be a correct
execution. State those independently.

  71: ## Legacy/shared-market path
  72: 
  73: **Current but pending retirement from the trader runtime.**
  74: 
  75: The shared path includes `SharedMarketSource`, `SharedMarketConsumer`,
  76: `SharedAnalysisDispatcher`, cutover/readiness logic, and local historical
  77: tables such as `shared_market_event_delivery`, `shared_market_consumer_state`,
  78: and `shared_market_health`. These records remain evidence and must not be
  79: dropped, reset, or used to manufacture an approval.
  80: 
  81: The collector event/cursor source is `crypto_ai_v2.market_data_stream_event`
  82: and `market_data_stream_cursor`. In the target local-candle runtime, the
  83: trader must not connect to, read, or write these collector tables.
  84: 
  85: `V103__fix_149_fresh_admission_indexes` is an existing Java Flyway migration
  86: that requires the collector event table for a fresh installation. A trader-only
  87: bootstrap policy is therefore **pending** and remains a release blocker. Do
  88: not edit applied Flyway migrations or Flyway history.
  89: 
  90: ## Implemented, unverified: local-candle architecture (FIX-153)
  91: 
  92: The implemented intended mode is `shared-market.mode=OFF` with trader-owned Binance kline
  93: ingestion and local candle writes. The shared executors and direct-ingestion
  94: path must never run together.
  95: 
  96: Implemented safeguards:
  97: 
  98: - Candle writes are monotonic: a late open update cannot reopen or overwrite a
  99:   closed candle.
 100: - A closed-candle transition is admitted exactly once using an atomic upsert
 101:   result plus in-process admission coordination.
 102: - A bounded local detector recovers a closed candle that was committed before
 103:   the in-memory event/dispatcher could start analysis.
 104: - Fresh candles may execute; stale candles are analysed historically only, or
 105:   their already-owned work is expired without business execution.
 106: - Analysis lanes are bounded. Under overload, 1m may retain only the latest
 107:   pending candle; higher intervals use an explicit bounded FIFO policy.
 108: - Historic shared `REVIEW_REQUIRED` evidence must not block OFF-mode work.
 109: - OFF-mode health/admin endpoints must use local-candle health and must not
 110:   query retired shared-market tables.
 111: - Current REST backfill can finalise an interrupted open row but cannot mint a
 112:   runtime close token or dispatch analysis. Runtime close tokens plus
 113:   provenance keep backfill out of detector admission. The approved, pending
 114:   automatic-reconciliation extension will also insert an exact wholly absent
 115:   candle only inside the active quality window, with `BACKFILL` provenance and
 116:   the same no-token/no-dispatch boundary.
 117: - Observed local behavior (2026-10-09): a WebSocket reconnect at a candle-close
 118:   boundary can leave the already-persisted 1m/5m rows open because Binance does
 119:   not replay the final closed-kline event. The current detector recovers missing
 120:   analysis admission, not missing close facts. An authoritative, bounded REST
 121:   repair may therefore finalise the exact `closed=0` row or, under the approved
 122:   gap-backfill scope, insert an exact absent identity. It must preserve existing
 123:   provenance, use `BACKFILL` for an insertion, create no close-transition token,
 124:   and never dispatch historical work. Automatic reconciliation of this reconnect
 125:   case remains a FIX-153 release gate; the one-time local repair is evidence,
 126:   not proof that the gap is closed.
 127: - Approved pending reconciliation design: gap backfill is insert-only (no
 128:   duplicate-key update); it can never alter a live row that appears during a
 129:   REST request. Candidate selection is bounded to the active quality window;
 130:   terminal audit records are not retried. Every candle/work route must produce
 131:   a durable terminal outcome or remain explicitly retryable after a transient
 132:   failure. Historical-only processing has no execution authority.
 133: - The pending universal mutation barrier is an in-memory drain participant,
 134:   not a database or persistent trading fence. Outside drain it must not delay,
 135:   queue, or block fresh trading, signals, or protection. Open-position
 136:   protection during application replacement remains an unresolved release gate.
 137: - Local source now contains the first reconciliation implementation slice:
 138:   V107 durable audit/outcome tables, update-only authoritative open-row repair,
 139:   pure insert-only gap backfill, a dedicated recovery executor, a reconnect
 140:   request hook, and drain participation. It is disabled by default and remains
 141:   unvalidated on MySQL; it has no deployment approval.
 142: - Direct prices are normalised to `DECIMAL(30,12)` before persistence,
 143:   protection and completion. Equal timestamps have one canonical receipt.
 144: - Every processing attempt is freshness-checked after normal locks using the
 145:   database-to-exchange correction. JVM-origin timestamp decisions use the
 146:   separately measured JVM-to-exchange correction. The measurement performs no
 147:   HTTP under execution locks and uses a bounded five-second time-only client.
 148:   General Binance REST calls use the configured request timeout, and scheduled
 149:   clock sampling has a four-thread Spring scheduler pool.
 150:   Bootstrap obtains time/klines before opening its local candle-write
 151:   transaction, so a stalled REST request does not retain database resources.
 152:   REST bootstrap gets Binance server time before klines.
 153: - An ADMIN-only drain stops analysis admission, exits the JVM on successful
 154:   quiesce, and resumes admission on timeout. Price protection pauses during
 155:   the controlled drain window.
 156: 
 157: ## Implemented, unverified: protection price-event state machine
 158: 
 159: For direct 1m price observations, the target evidence lifecycle is:
 160: 
 161: ```text
 162: PENDING
 163:   -> APPLIED                 (protection effects and state commit together)
 164:   -> NON_CANONICAL           (invalid, stale, out-of-order, or duplicate)
 165:   -> PROTECTION_NOT_APPLIED  (confirmed rollback/crash resolution)
 166: ```
 167: 
 168: Replay and price authority consume only accepted `LEGACY`/`APPLIED` rows.
 169: Replay must reject a parity claim when the requested range contains unresolved
 170: direct `PENDING` evidence; this must not block live trading.
 171: 
 172: The automatic resolver is valid only for the paper-trading phase, where every
 173: protection effect commits in the same transaction as its `APPLIED` update.
 174: Before deployment, the code must prove that there are no asynchronous,
 175: `REQUIRES_NEW`, in-memory-only, or external effects in this boundary. A future
 176: live-exchange order needs a separate idempotent/exchange-reconciliation design.
 177: 
 178: The target runtime also requires exactly one active trader process. This is an
 179: operational prerequisite, not a database lease or fence.
 180: 
 181: ## Pending: FIX-154 higher-timeframe BUY validation
 182: 
 183: FIX-154 is separate from the local-candle change and is not implemented.
 184: 
 185: Its purpose is to let a historical bearish 1h signal affect a current 1m BUY
 186: only when the historical evidence is fresh, quality-valid, and sufficiently
 187: strong. `btcContextEntryAllowed=false` on a historical signal is investigatory
 188: evidence, not a higher-timeframe quality gate; the current 1m BTC protection
 189: remains unchanged.
 190: 
 191: The design includes reliability bands (`NOT_TRUSTED`, `SOFT_CONFLICT`,
 192: `HARD_BEARISH_CANDIDATE`), required fresh/quality-valid bearish 5m support for
 193: a hard veto, persisted `trade_signal.data_quality_valid`, recovery release
 194: rules, immutable outcome audit evidence, and Replay/no-look-ahead parity.
 195: 
 196: The implementation design is maintained in `codex-docs/FIX-154_TECHNICAL_DESIGN.md`.
 197: It supersedes no existing deployed behavior and is deliberately separate from
 198: the unrelated legacy readiness document under `src/main/resources/md/FIX-146.md`.
 199: 
 200: ## Deployment posture
 201: 
 202: Neither FIX-153 nor FIX-154 is deployment-ready. FIX-153 source hardening is
 203: implemented but unverified; FIX-154 remains pending.
 204: 
 205: Required validation includes Java 21 build/tests, disposable MySQL bootstrap,
 206: real-MySQL concurrency and lock-wait tests, crash/restart tests, stale-input
 207: tests, Replay parity checks, OFF-mode health/admin checks, collector-free
 208: runtime verification, deterministic dispatcher/detector/drain tests,
 209: two-process Windows lock rehearsal, and sustained-load observation across
 210: enabled symbols and intervals. This local workspace has Java 17 and cannot
 211: compile the Java 21 project.
 212: 
 213: No production configuration, database, service, or deployment change is made
 214: without explicit user approval.

 216: ## FIX-153 validation status (2026-10-09)
 217: 
 218: The reconciliation component now has deterministic Java 21 coverage for its
 219: core admission and outcome contract. The tests execute the real audit and
 220: outcome stores against H2 while mocking only Binance and the candle write
 221: boundary. They prove that healthy delayed live closes are not taken over and
 222: that recovery remains token-free/non-live when it is positively evidenced.
 223: 
 224: The real-MySQL suite contains matching update-only and insert-only assertions,
 225: but it requires a deliberately disposable loopback MySQL instance and is not
 226: run by the ordinary unit-test goal. This is a release gate, not a warning that
 227: can be waived. The shared Binance 429/418 admission gate, universal mutation
 228: barrier, structural historical-only isolation, financial-effect reconciler,
 229: atomicity/crash proofs, replacement-time position protection, Replay parity,
 230: and soak validation remain incomplete. Therefore `local-candle.reconciliation.enabled`
 231: must stay `false`.
 232: 
 233: The single `local-candle` configuration mapping is a startup invariant. It now
 234: contains both reconciliation and existing local-runtime properties; a second
 235: mapping is invalid YAML and prevents the Spring application context from
 236: starting.
 237: 
 238: ### Shared Binance REST admission
 239: 
 240: `BinanceRestAdmissionGate` owns one process-wide REST cooldown. It is consulted
 241: immediately before every call through `BinanceMarketDataClient`; a 429/418
 242: response extends the cooldown using `Retry-After` when it is supplied, otherwise
 243: the bounded fallback. This protects all local REST consumers from repeatedly
 244: calling Binance during a rate-limit/ban response. It is deliberately not part
 245: of the WebSocket or protection path and is not a persisted trading fence.
 246: 
 247: ### Outcome-schema startup invariant
 248: 
 249: The active signal-processing runtime writes `candle_analysis_outcome` for
 250: terminal analysis evidence. V108 therefore ships with the FIX-154 release even
 251: though local-candle reconciliation remains disabled. `CandleAnalysisOutcomeSchemaVerifier`
 252: runs after Flyway and fails application startup with a clear message if the
 253: table is absent; this prevents later processing transactions from failing only
 254: when they attempt their first outcome write.
 255: # FIX-154 implementation update Г?" 2026-10-10
 256: 
 257: `HigherTimeframeBuyAssessmentService` is the single pure assessment boundary for
 258: the 5m/1h BUY context. It returns effective decisions separately from the JPA
 259: entities, so a SOFT 1h conflict can be assessed as effective `NEUTRAL` without
 260: ever changing the persisted signal. `TradeExecutionValidationService` uses it
 261: for direct BUY and accumulated-evidence authority; `OpportunityConsolidationService`
 262: uses the same assessment for consolidation. A trusted SOFT bearish 1h limits an
 263: initial entry to 25%; a trusted HARD or unknown bearish 1h rejects it, while
 264: the legacy 5m bearish veto keeps priority.
 265: 
 266: `buy_htf_assessment_audit` is append-only operational evidence. Its writer is
 267: best-effort and uses a bounded dedicated executor: auditing never borrows an
 268: execution transaction's database connection, is skipped in Replay, and cannot
 269: be part of a BUY decision. The progressive add route retains its
 270: existing raw-1h guard; it writes `SOFT_HTF_ADD_BLOCKED` evidence only after
 271: that guard has already rejected an add.
 272: 
 273: `GET /api/fix154/health` exposes non-gating counters for untrusted bearish
 274: blocks, soft caps, soft add blocks, and best-effort audit failures.
 275: 
 276: ## FIX-153 automatic local-candle reconciliation Г?" enabled 2026-10-10
 277: 
 278: In `shared-market.mode=OFF`, `LocalCandleReconciliationService` runs every
 279: five seconds on its dedicated single-worker executor. It finds eligible
 280: missing or interrupted candle identities inside the data-quality window, reads
 281: the authoritative Binance candle, and writes only verified final evidence.
 282: An existing open row is finalized by an update-only path; a missing row uses a
 283: plain insert-if-absent backfill path. Neither route creates a close token,
 284: dispatches analysis, or executes a trade. The next genuine live close resumes
 285: ordinary analysis after the quality window is complete.

 159:   with and without those cases. Compute the floor per trade as
 160:   `max(original_lock - tolerance, fee_adjusted_breakeven)` and report when
 161:   breakeven binds. Compare A and B as paired outcomes on the same eligible
 162:   breach events, reporting per-event B-minus-A and the count of later declines
 163:   avoided by A.
 164: 
 165: # Replay-versus-Production parity audit Г?" 2026-10-10
 166: 
 167: - Scope: source-level comparison of the manual Regression/Replay pipeline with
 168:   the current paper-trading Production path. No trading code, configuration,
 169:   database data, or Replay result was changed.
 170: - Confirmed shared authority: Replay regenerates technical indicators through
 171:   `TechnicalIndicatorService`, signals through `AnalysisService`, BUY authority
 172:   through `ExecutionIntelligenceService`, BUY/SELL validation through
 173:   `TradeExecutionValidationService`, and normal exit, TP-continuation,
 174:   profit-lock, and near-TP policies through the corresponding shared policy
 175:   classes. When canonical `LEGACY`/`APPLIED` price events exist, the Replay
 176:   consumes them in timestamp order before making the same close-candle signal
 177:   visible, matching the documented live ordering.
 178: - Confirmed boundary: Replay is a shadow simulation, not a transactionally
 179:   identical copy of Production. It starts with fixed capital of 10,000 USDT,
 180:   manages one symbol/position in isolation, uses replay-local daily budget and
 181:   position state, and writes only `*_test` tables. It therefore cannot
 182:   reproduce an actual wallet balance, simultaneous positions, global
 183:   `maxOpenPositions`, daily loss limit, idempotency races, database locks, or
 184:   real execution latency.
 185: - Confirmed historical-evidence limitation: derivatives history is not
 186:   persisted, so historical Replay always receives `UNAVAILABLE` derivatives
 187:   context when that feature is enabled. Historical order-book evaluation uses
 188:   stored snapshots only and becomes `UNAVAILABLE` when no snapshot exists,
 189:   whereas live Production samples its in-memory/live Binance source. Such runs
 190:   are useful simulations but are not full signal-parity proof unless the
 191:   required historical evidence exists and is reported.
 192: - Confirmed price-evidence limitation: a Replay run labels itself
 193:   `EXACT_PRICE_REPLAY` whenever at least one accepted price event exists. It
 194:   does not prove complete tick coverage for every time an open position needed
 195:   protection. Windows with no accepted events fall back to signal prices and
 196:   are labelled `SIGNAL_PRICE_FALLBACK`; neither fallback nor partial coverage
 197:   should be described as tick-exact reproduction.
 198: - Test evidence: Java 21 focused tests passed for profit-lock/TP-extension
 199:   parity, position exit/continuation, near-TP policy, and shared sizing.
 200:   Existing Replay-specific coverage is narrow: it does not execute a complete
 201:   Production-versus-Replay scenario across entry, add, wallet controls,
 202:   price-event ordering, partial harvest, and exit.
 203: - Conclusion: Replay is suitable for controlled, manual strategy regression
 204:   and the approved FIX-155 research work only when each run carries explicit
 205:   evidence-quality labels. It is not yet valid to claim it is fully identical
 206:   to Production in all phases. A future parity program must add deterministic
 207:   scenario tests and a run-level eligibility contract before using Replay as a
 208:   release-equivalence certificate.

  10: 
  11: ## 1. Fixed scope and earned results
  12: 
  13: FIX-156 changes **Replay only**. It does not change Production source,
  14: behaviour, database writes, account state, schedulers, HTTP traffic, or
  15: latency. Replay is a manual single-symbol research tool with fixed notional
  16: output. It is not a wallet, balance, cash, reserve, budget, portfolio, or
  17: historical-fill simulator.
  18: 
  19: A run has two independent earned certification dimensions:
  20: 
  21: - `ANALYSIS_PARITY`: a qualified Production signal/outcome is reproduced
  22:   using as-of evidence.
  23: - `LIFECYCLE_PARITY`: a qualified recorded-entry lifecycle passes the
  24:   separate lifecycle metric and critical-safety gate.
  25: 
  26: A run may earn neither, one, or both dimensions. `REFUSED_INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`
  27: and `FAILED_REPLAY` are terminal states which prevent either claim.
  28: `FAILED_REPLAY` is only for a technical error, cancellation, or failed
  29: staging. A business mismatch is published as parity-not-earned with its first
  30: divergence; it is not a technical failure.
  31: 
  32: No result may claim wallet, account, exact-fill, live-scheduling, MySQL-lock,
  33: or Binance-availability parity.
  34: 
  35: ## 2. Decided owner rules
  36: 
  37: | Decision | Implementable rule |
  38: | --- | --- |
  39: | O-1 | Replay never calls `wallet_settings` or shared `validateBuy`. A Replay-local BUY mirror reads only a frozen policy profile. |
  40: | O-2 | Signal and lifecycle parity are separate certification dimensions. |
  41: | O-3 | Every class reachable from a Replay request or worker is inside the boundary. |
  42: | O-4 | The 99% result is separate per metric, based on a frozen lower confidence bound, coverage floor, and critical-safety gate. |
  43: | O-5 | A lifecycle fixture carries the full recorded timeline, not entry only. |
  44: | O-6 | No separate Replay database identity/datasource is introduced. |

  94: 
  95: ## 6. Mandatory logging registry
  96: 
  97: There is one registry only. Every Replay log starts
  98: `[FIX-156][REPLAY]`, includes `runId`, `profileHash`, `baselineHash`,
  99: `symbol`, and when present `fixtureId`, `signalId`, and `priceEventId`.
 100: Every time is displayed as stored UTC **and** KSA (`+03:00`). No credential,
 101: token, account number, raw SQL parameter, or unbounded payload is logged.
 102: 
 103: The only event IDs are:
 104: 
 105: - `RUN_REQUESTED`, `RUN_QUALIFIED`, `RUN_REFUSED`, `RUN_FAILED`, `RUN_PROMOTED`;
 106: - `FIXTURE_LOADED`;
 107: - `PRICE_SPAN`;
 108: - `DECISION`;
 109: - `FIRST_DIVERGENCE`;
 110: - `FORBIDDEN_DEPENDENCY`; and
 111: - `POLICY_FINGERPRINT`.
 112: 
 113: Event payloads include the RPR-0.9.10 required fields: reason/evidence counts,
 114: fixture hash/count, price-span boundaries/gap/refusal, decision path and
 115: Section-3.3.1 step, input event IDs, expected/actual first divergence, attempted
 116: class/method/table/URL, and policy source/configuration/profile identity.
 117: Volume is bounded by E05. Tests assert one correctly correlated event per
 118: occurrence.
 119: 
 120: A critical-safety mismatch is `ERROR` and **parity-not-earned**. Its mismatch
 121: certificate and first divergence are published. It never becomes
 122: `FAILED_REPLAY` merely because the result disagrees. `FAILED_REPLAY` means
 123: technical error/cancellation/failed staging and discards staged artifacts.
 124: 
 125: ## 7. Numbered validation matrix
 126: 
 127: | Test ID | Required assertion |
 128: | --- | --- |
 129: | T156-01 | 1m/5m/1h SELL and active-profit-lock SELL suppression match Production. |
 130: | T156-02a | Signal-path TP, profit-lock, stop-loss and hard-floor precedence matches Section 3.3.1. |
 131: | T156-02b | Price-path TP, stop-loss, dynamic lock, rebase floor, lock breach, normal exit and near-TP precedence matches Section 3.3.1. |
 132: | T156-03 | Equal-time prices retain `(observed_at,id)`; E07 availability time governs same-boundary signal order. |
 133: | T156-04 | Qualified price tail drains through `executionEnd`; incomplete tail refuses; after-end events are ignored. |
 134: | T156-05 | Entry fixture execution time controls gating; no Replay request queries account tables. |
 135: | T156-05a | Missing/malformed/wrong-date/fingerprint-mismatched policy profile is non-comparable/refused; no fallback to current settings. |
 136: | T156-05b | Full timeline fixture covers add, stop/TP change, extension, harvest and profit-lock transition; first divergence ends that lifecycle metric. |
 137: | T156-05c | Replay-local BUY mirror matches each recorded Production BUY allow/reject decision in the development fixture set, or publishes a mismatch without calling shared validation. |
 138: | T156-06 | Lock-active positions do not evaluate/add when Production skips it. |
 139: | T156-07a | Dynamic profit lock toggle on and off, values, extension and rebase match the profile fixtures. |
 140: | T156-07b | Near-TP consumes dated exchange constraints and makes no HTTP/Binance call. |
 141: | T156-08 | Missing historical context/data-quality/configuration evidence produces the right refusal/exclusion/bucket. |
 142: | T156-08a | Missing or non-as-of sentiment provider configuration/health or prior indicator snapshot refuses analysis parity; no current value is substituted. |
 143: | T156-09 | Direct and async account/HTTP/fallback access emits `FORBIDDEN_DEPENDENCY` and publishes nothing. |
 144: | T156-09a | Static reachability/architecture test rejects any Replay-reachable repository, JDBC template, table-name access or HTTP client outside the approved allow-list. |
 145: | T156-09b | Replay-owned table allow-list test rejects every read/write outside approved market-evidence and Replay-owned tables. |
 146: | T156-09c | Replay output/diagnostics expose only Replay fixture or position keys, never `paper_position_id` or another account identifier. |
 147: | T156-09d | Entry consumption handles both cases: source-row signals use their saved IDs; `analyzeForRegression` signals use a stable Replay-owned key. A repeated entry is consumed without account evidence reads/writes. |
 148: | T156-10 | Legacy/experimental observers cannot change a baseline result. |
 149: | T156-11 | Charts/output query only Replay-owned data plus immutable overlay. |
 150: | T156-12 | Ordinary and critical mismatches publish the correct first divergence; critical mismatches prevent the affected parity claim without becoming technical failure. |
 151: | T156-13 | Replay-open/Production-open is censored as `OPEN_AT_REPLAY_END` with the final qualified mark price, price-event ID and time; Replay-open/Production-closed is a mismatch. No synthetic exit is created. |
 152: | T156-14 | Staging/cancellation/resource refusal has correct terminal result and artifact handling. |
 153: | T156-15 | Logging emits only the Section 6 event IDs, once per occurrence, with required UTC+KSA correlation fields. |
 154: | T156-16 | Disposable-MySQL migration/schema validation is mandatory in the release stage and cannot silently skip. |

 156: ## 8. Completion criteria
 157: 
 158: Before any parity claim, actual changes must reconcile to the approved registry;
 159: all required tests and E01-E10 evidence must exist; the qualified/excluded/
 160: refused/non-comparable/censored buckets must be reported by cause and exit
 161: class; and the frozen coverage/count/lower-bound requirements must pass
 162: separately for both dimensions.
 163: 
 164: There must be **zero unexplained critical-safety mismatches** in stop-loss,
 165: profit-lock, take-profit, near-TP ownership and duplicate-exit classes. A
 166: qualified cohort may earn its applicable `ANALYSIS_PARITY` and/or
 167: `LIFECYCLE_PARITY` dimension only. It never earns account or exact-fill parity.

 171: E01 and E02 are now consolidated into this preparation document. They are

 176: ### E01 - dependency audit: confirmed current violations
 177: 
 178: The current Replay path is not inside the approved boundary yet:
 179: 
 180: - `wallet_settings` is Replay-reachable through `ShadowProductionReplayService`,
 181:   `OneCandleContinuationGraceReplayObserver`, and shared BUY validation.
 182: - Near-TP reaches live Binance `/api/v3/exchangeInfo` through
 183:   `BinanceMinimumExecutionPolicy`.
 184: - `wallet_trade` is read by the all-trades chart and proven-trade enrichment.
 185: - If Replay scope propagation is absent, `EntryConsumptionPolicy` and
 186:   `StopLossEvidenceStore` can fall through to Production-account reads.
 187: - Replay currently writes the shared `fix122_evaluation` table and can write
 188:   `shared_candle_input_audit` in shared-market LIVE mode.
 189: 
 190: The required future response is Replay-local policy/data adapters, immutable
 191: policy and exchange-constraint fixtures, the allow-listed Replay data-access
 192: layer, static reachability checks, and direct/async rejection tests. The E01
 193: audit must also decide whether every shared-table write is replaced by a
 194: Replay-owned record or made unreachable in the baseline.
 195: 
 196: RPR-0.9.11 records these formal boundary rows. They are not merely audit notes
 197: because each one must be closed, tested and reconciled:
 198: 
 199: | Proposed row | E01 boundary violation | Required disposition |
 200: | --- | --- | --- |
 201: | D47 | `OneCandleContinuationGraceReplayObserver` reads `wallet_settings`. | Remove from baseline invocation or feed only the frozen Replay policy profile. |
 202: | D48 | Replay writes shared `fix122_evaluation`. | Replace with Replay-owned evidence/output or make the path unreachable in a baseline run. |
 203: | D49 | Replay can write shared `shared_candle_input_audit` when shared-market mode is LIVE. | Make the path unreachable in baseline Replay; prove OFF/LIVE mode cannot bypass the boundary. |
 204: | D50 | Missing Replay scope can fall through through `EntryConsumptionPolicy` to account evidence. | Fail closed through scope propagation and the Replay access allow-list. |
 205: | D51 | Missing Replay scope can fall through through `StopLossEvidenceStore.latest` to `wallet_trade`. | Fail closed through scope propagation and the Replay access allow-list. |
 206: | D52 | Missing scope can fall through to shared `execution_opportunity` reads/writes. | Route only to Replay-owned state or reject; never use shared mutable opportunity state. |
 207: | D53 | Replay can read current sentiment-provider weights/health while evaluating historical time. | Require a dated immutable sentiment-provider configuration/health fixture; otherwise refuse analysis parity. |
 208: | D54 | Replay can depend on a Production-saved prior indicator snapshot; a missing snapshot changes its result. | Include exact prior-snapshot identity/availability in the evidence qualifier; refuse when absent or not historically available. |

 399:     private LivePriceEvaluation evaluateLivePrice(long runId, String symbol, ShadowPosition p,

 418:                                 "entry={}, oldTp={}, newTp={}, highest={}, profitLockActive={}, profitLockPrice={}, previousState={}, state={}, " +

 725:     private ShadowPosition profitLockState(ShadowPosition p, BigDecimal price) {
 726:         WalletSettings settings = walletSettings();
 727:         BigDecimal activation = nvl(settings.getProfitLockActivationPercent(), BigDecimal.valueOf(70));
 728:         BigDecimal highest = p.highest() == null ? price : p.highest().max(price);
 729:         BigDecimal progress = progressPercent(p.entryPrice(), p.takeProfit(), highest);
 730: 
 731:         if (p.profitLockState() == ProfitLockState.TP_EXTENSION_REBASE
 732:                 && progress.compareTo(activation) < 0) {
 733:             // Replay parity with Production FIX-118: preserve the historical lock/legacy flag,
 734:             // but keep it non-executable until the new TP geometry earns activation again.
 735:             return p.withLock(highest, true, p.profitLockPrice(), ProfitLockState.TP_EXTENSION_REBASE,
 736:                     p.profitLockRebaseStartedAt());
 737:         }
 738: 
 739:         // FIX-118 parity: when REBASE earns activation, rebuild the lock from the current
 740:         // TP geometry instead of retaining the superseded pre-extension lock.
 741:         boolean freshGeometryActivation = p.profitLockState() == ProfitLockState.TP_EXTENSION_REBASE;
 742:         ProfitLockPolicy.State state = profitLockPolicy.evaluate(
 743:                 p.entryPrice(), p.takeProfit(), price, highest,
 744:                 freshGeometryActivation ? false : (p.profitLockState() == ProfitLockState.ACTIVE || p.profitLockActive()),
 745:                 freshGeometryActivation ? null : p.profitLockPrice(),
 746:                 settings.isDynamicProfitLockEnabled(), activation,
 747:                 nvl(settings.getProfitLockInitialPercent(), BigDecimal.valueOf(40)),
 748:                 nvl(settings.getProfitLockTrailStepPercent(), BigDecimal.valueOf(10)));
 749:         ProfitLockState nextState = state.active() ? ProfitLockState.ACTIVE : ProfitLockState.INACTIVE;
 750:         return p.withLock(state.highestPrice(), state.active(), state.lockPrice(), nextState, null);
 751:     }

 753:     private ShadowPosition rebaseForExtendedTarget(ShadowPosition p, BigDecimal newTarget, BigDecimal extensionPrice, Instant at) {
 754:         if (p == null || newTarget == null) return p;
 755:         BigDecimal oldTarget = p.takeProfit();
 756:         BigDecimal oldLock = p.profitLockPrice();
 757:         BigDecimal activation = nvl(walletSettings().getProfitLockActivationPercent(), BigDecimal.valueOf(70));
 758:         BigDecimal extensionHighest = p.highest() == null ? p.entryPrice() : p.highest();
 759:         if (extensionPrice != null && extensionPrice.compareTo(extensionHighest) > 0) extensionHighest = extensionPrice;
 760:         ShadowPosition withExtensionHigh = p.withLock(extensionHighest, p.profitLockActive(), p.profitLockPrice(),
 761:                 p.profitLockState(), p.profitLockRebaseStartedAt());
 762:         BigDecimal progress = progressPercent(p.entryPrice(), newTarget, extensionHighest);
 763:         if (p.profitLockState() == ProfitLockState.ACTIVE) {
 764:             if (progress.compareTo(activation) < 0) {
 765:                 ShadowPosition rebasing = withExtensionHigh.withLock(extensionHighest, true, p.profitLockPrice(), ProfitLockState.TP_EXTENSION_REBASE,
 766:                         at == null ? Instant.now() : at);
 767:                 log.info("[FIX-120][REPLAY][TP_GEOMETRY_REBASE] positionId={}, previousState={}, newState={}, oldTarget={}, newTarget={}, " +
 768:                                 "extensionPrice={}, highest={}, newGeometryProgressPct={}, oldLock={}, freshLock={}, activationPct={}, geometryRebased=true",
 769:                         p.positionId(), p.profitLockState(), rebasing.profitLockState(), oldTarget, newTarget, extensionPrice,
 770:                         extensionHighest, progress, oldLock, rebasing.profitLockPrice(), activation);
 771:                 return rebasing;
 772:             }
 773:             // FIX-120 Production/Replay parity: the old executable lock belongs to the
 774:             // superseded TP geometry. If the extended winner still qualifies, establish a
 775:             // fresh geometry baseline. Raw extensionPrice is current; extensionHighest is the
 776:             // historical-best seed; previousActive/previousLock are deliberately discarded.
 777:             WalletSettings settings = walletSettings();
 778:             BigDecimal currentForPolicy = extensionPrice == null ? extensionHighest : extensionPrice;
 779:             ProfitLockPolicy.State rebased = profitLockPolicy.evaluate(
 780:                     p.entryPrice(), newTarget, currentForPolicy, extensionHighest,
 781:                     false, null, settings.isDynamicProfitLockEnabled(), activation,
 782:                     nvl(settings.getProfitLockInitialPercent(), BigDecimal.valueOf(40)),
 783:                     nvl(settings.getProfitLockTrailStepPercent(), BigDecimal.valueOf(10)));
 784:             if (rebased.active()) {
 785:                 ShadowPosition active = withExtensionHigh.withLock(rebased.highestPrice(), true, rebased.lockPrice(), ProfitLockState.ACTIVE, null);
 786:                 log.info("[FIX-120][REPLAY][TP_GEOMETRY_REBASE] positionId={}, previousState={}, newState={}, oldTarget={}, newTarget={}, " +
 787:                                 "extensionPrice={}, highest={}, newGeometryProgressPct={}, oldLock={}, freshLock={}, activationPct={}, geometryRebased=true",
 788:                         p.positionId(), p.profitLockState(), active.profitLockState(), oldTarget, newTarget, extensionPrice,
 789:                         rebased.highestPrice(), rebased.progressPercent(), oldLock, rebased.lockPrice(), activation);
 790:                 return active;

===== DynamicProfitLock 60-260 =====
  60:      * activation threshold again. This gives an approved continuation meaningful room
  61:      * without forgetting that profit protection had already been earned.
  62:      */
  63:     @Transactional
  64:     public Evaluation evaluatePrice(String symbolValue, BigDecimal currentPrice) {
  65:         if (symbolValue == null || symbolValue.isBlank() || currentPrice == null
  66:                 || currentPrice.signum() <= 0) {
  67:             return Evaluation.inactive("No valid market price is available.");
  68:         }
  69: 
  70:         String symbol = symbolValue.trim().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
  71:         WalletManagedPosition position = positionRepository
  72:                 .findFirstBySymbolAndStatusOrderByOpenedAtDesc(symbol, "OPEN")
  73:                 .orElse(null);
  74:         if (position == null) {
  75:             return Evaluation.inactive("No open wallet position exists.");
  76:         }
  77: 
  78:         WalletSettings settings = settings();
  79:         if (!settings.isDynamicProfitLockEnabled()) {
  80:             return Evaluation.inactive("Dynamic Profit Lock is disabled in Administration.");
  81:         }
  82: 
  83:         BigDecimal entry = position.getAverageEntryPriceUsdt();
  84:         BigDecimal target = position.getTakeProfitUsdt();
  85:         BigDecimal current = currentPrice;
  86:         if (entry == null || target == null || entry.signum() <= 0 || target.compareTo(entry) <= 0) {
  87:             return Evaluation.inactive("The position does not have a valid long take-profit distance.");
  88:         }
  89: 
  90:         ProfitLockProfile profile = configuredProfile(settings);
  91:         BigDecimal activation = profile.activationPercent();
  92:         BigDecimal initialLock = profile.initialLockPercent();
  93:         BigDecimal trailStep = profile.trailStepPercent();
  94:         BigDecimal previousHighest = position.getHighestPriceUsdt();
  95:         boolean previousPersistedActive = position.isProfitLockActive();
  96:         BigDecimal previousLock = position.getProfitLockPriceUsdt();
  97:         BigDecimal previousProgress = position.getProfitLockProgressPercent();
  98:         ProfitLockState previousState = normalizedState(position);
  99: 
 100:         BigDecimal highest = previousHighest == null ? current : previousHighest.max(current);
 101:         BigDecimal progress = progressPercent(entry, target, highest);
 102:         BigDecimal lockPrice = previousLock;
 103:         ProfitLockState state = previousState;
 104:         boolean executableActive;
 105:         boolean triggered;
 106: 
 107:         if (previousState == ProfitLockState.TP_EXTENSION_REBASE && progress.compareTo(activation) < 0) {
 108:             // Keep the legacy active flag/lock persisted so history is not lost, but do not
 109:             // allow the superseded geometry to trigger an exit during the rebase window.
 110:             executableActive = false;
 111:             triggered = false;
 112:         } else {
 113:             // FIX-118 refinement: when a TP-extension rebase earns activation against the
 114:             // CURRENT target, rebuild the executable lock from the current geometry instead
 115:             // of carrying the historical pre-extension lock through ProfitLockPolicy's
 116:             // monotonic previous-lock rule.
 117:             boolean freshGeometryActivation = previousState == ProfitLockState.TP_EXTENSION_REBASE;
 118:             ProfitLockPolicy.State policyState = profitLockPolicy.evaluate(
 119:                     entry, target, current, highest,
 120:                     freshGeometryActivation ? false : (previousState == ProfitLockState.ACTIVE || previousPersistedActive),
 121:                     freshGeometryActivation ? null : previousLock,
 122:                     true, activation, initialLock, trailStep);
 123:             highest = policyState.highestPrice();
 124:             progress = policyState.progressPercent();
 125:             lockPrice = policyState.lockPrice();
 126:             executableActive = policyState.active();
 127:             triggered = policyState.triggered();
 128:             state = executableActive ? ProfitLockState.ACTIVE : ProfitLockState.INACTIVE;
 129:         }
 130: 
 131:         // During REBASE the legacy flag intentionally remains true: protection was historically
 132:         // earned. The explicit state is now the sole execution authority.
 133:         boolean persistedActive = state == ProfitLockState.TP_EXTENSION_REBASE
 134:                 ? true
 135:                 : executableActive;
 136: 
 137:         Instant activatedAt = position.getProfitLockActivatedAt();
 138:         if (persistedActive && activatedAt == null) activatedAt = Instant.now();
 139:         Instant rebaseStartedAt = state == ProfitLockState.TP_EXTENSION_REBASE
 140:                 ? position.getProfitLockRebaseStartedAt()
 141:                 : null;
 142: 
 143:         boolean changed = position.getHighestPriceUsdt() == null
 144:                 || highest.compareTo(position.getHighestPriceUsdt()) != 0
 145:                 || position.isProfitLockActive() != persistedActive
 146:                 || different(position.getProfitLockPriceUsdt(), lockPrice)
 147:                 || different(position.getProfitLockProgressPercent(), progress)
 148:                 || position.getProfitLockState() != state
 149:                 || !java.util.Objects.equals(position.getProfitLockRebaseStartedAt(), rebaseStartedAt)
 150:                 || (position.getProfitLockActivatedAt() == null && activatedAt != null);
 151: 
 152:         if (changed) {
 153:             position.setHighestPriceUsdt(highest);
 154:             position.setProfitLockActive(persistedActive);
 155:             position.setProfitLockPriceUsdt(lockPrice);
 156:             position.setProfitLockProgressPercent(progress);
 157:             position.setProfitLockActivatedAt(activatedAt);
 158:             position.setProfitLockState(state);
 159:             position.setProfitLockRebaseStartedAt(rebaseStartedAt);
 160:             position.setUpdatedAt(Instant.now());
 161:             positionRepository.save(position);
 162:         }
 163: 
 164:         BigDecimal hardProfitFloor = entry.multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(1.0005));
 165:         boolean hardFloorTriggered = state == ProfitLockState.TP_EXTENSION_REBASE
 166:                 && current.compareTo(hardProfitFloor) < 0;
 167: 
 168:         if (changed || triggered || hardFloorTriggered || previousState != state) {
 169:             log.info("[FIX-118][PRODUCTION][PROFIT_LOCK_EVAL] positionId={}, symbol={}, current={}, entry={}, target={}, " +
 170:                             "previousHighest={}, highest={}, previousState={}, state={}, previousPersistedActive={}, persistedActive={}, " +
 171:                             "previousLock={}, lock={}, previousProgressPct={}, progressPct={}, activationPct={}, triggered={}, " +
 172:                             "hardFloor={}, hardFloorTriggered={}, persisted={}",
 173:                     position.getId(), symbol, current, entry, target,
 174:                     previousHighest, highest, previousState, state, previousPersistedActive, persistedActive,
 175:                     previousLock, lockPrice, previousProgress, progress, activation, triggered,
 176:                     hardProfitFloor, hardFloorTriggered, changed);
 177:         }
 178: 
 179:         String profileText = " Admin profile=" + profile.name() +
 180:                 " (activation=" + activation.stripTrailingZeros().toPlainString() + "%, initial lock=" +
 181:                 initialLock.stripTrailingZeros().toPlainString() + "%, trail=" +
 182:                 trailStep.stripTrailingZeros().toPlainString() + "%).";
 183:         String explanation;
 184:         if (hardFloorTriggered) {
 185:             explanation = "TP-extension rebase is active and price " + current
 186:                     + " breached the protected-profit safety floor " + hardProfitFloor + "." + profileText;
 187:         } else if (state == ProfitLockState.TP_EXTENSION_REBASE) {
 188:             explanation = "Profit Lock is rebasing to the extended take-profit geometry; the historical lock "
 189:                     + lockPrice + " remains persisted but is non-executable. Current best progress is "
 190:                     + progress.setScale(2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP) + "% and reactivation starts at "
 191:                     + activation.stripTrailingZeros().toPlainString() + "%." + profileText;
 192:         } else if (triggered) {
 193:             explanation = "Price " + current + " reached the protected profit-lock level " + lockPrice
 194:                     + " after the position had reached " + progress.setScale(2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP)
 195:                     + "% of its take-profit distance." + profileText;
 196:         } else if (executableActive) {

 199:         } else {

 203:         }
 204: 
 205:         return new Evaluation(true, executableActive, triggered, position.getId(), current, highest,

 209:     /**
 210:      * FIX-120 correction/refinement to FIX-118. Called in the same transaction that persists the new TP.
 211:      * A TP change invalidates the prior executable lock as a calculation baseline. If current
 212:      * best progress remains at/above activation, stay ACTIVE but derive a fresh lock from the
 213:      * new geometry using raw extensionPrice as current and extensionHighest as the historical
 214:      * best seed. If progress falls below activation, preserve the historical lock for audit but
 215:      * make it non-executable in TP_EXTENSION_REBASE until the current geometry requalifies.
 216:      */
 217:     public ExtensionTransition onTakeProfitExtended(WalletManagedPosition position, BigDecimal newTarget, BigDecimal extensionPrice, Instant changedAt) {
 218:         if (position == null || newTarget == null || position.getAverageEntryPriceUsdt() == null) {
 219:             return ExtensionTransition.none();
 220:         }
 221:         ProfitLockState previousState = normalizedState(position);
 222:         BigDecimal oldTarget = position.getTakeProfitUsdt();
 223:         BigDecimal oldLock = position.getProfitLockPriceUsdt();
 224:         BigDecimal extensionHighest = position.getHighestPriceUsdt() == null
 225:                 ? position.getAverageEntryPriceUsdt()
 226:                 : position.getHighestPriceUsdt();
 227:         if (extensionPrice != null && extensionPrice.compareTo(extensionHighest) > 0) {
 228:             extensionHighest = extensionPrice;
 229:             position.setHighestPriceUsdt(extensionHighest);
 230:         }
 231:         BigDecimal progress = progressPercent(position.getAverageEntryPriceUsdt(), newTarget, extensionHighest);
 232:         BigDecimal activation = configuredProfile(settings()).activationPercent();
 233:         ProfitLockState nextState = previousState;
 234:         // TP changed now, so persist progress against the new geometry immediately even though
 235:         // the extension tick returns before the next normal Profit Lock evaluation.
 236:         position.setProfitLockProgressPercent(progress);
 237: 
 238:         if (previousState == ProfitLockState.ACTIVE) {
 239:             if (progress.compareTo(activation) < 0) {
 240:                 nextState = ProfitLockState.TP_EXTENSION_REBASE;
 241:                 position.setProfitLockState(nextState);
 242:                 position.setProfitLockRebaseStartedAt(changedAt == null ? Instant.now() : changedAt);
 243:                 // Legacy compatibility flag deliberately stays true; ProfitLockState is the sole
 244:                 // authority for whether the persisted historical lock may execute.
 245:                 position.setProfitLockActive(true);
 246:             } else {
 247:                 // FIX-120: the extension still leaves the winner beyond activation, but the old
 248:                 // lock belongs to the superseded TP geometry. Establish a fresh geometry baseline.
 249:                 // Deliberately pass raw extensionPrice as current and extensionHighest as previous
 250:                 // highest: ProfitLockPolicy then sees the real boundary tick plus the authoritative
 251:                 // best price, while previousActive/previousLock are intentionally discarded.
 252:                 ProfitLockProfile profile = configuredProfile(settings());
 253:                 BigDecimal currentForPolicy = extensionPrice == null ? extensionHighest : extensionPrice;
 254:                 ProfitLockPolicy.State rebased = profitLockPolicy.evaluate(
 255:                         position.getAverageEntryPriceUsdt(), newTarget, currentForPolicy, extensionHighest,
 256:                         false, null, true, profile.activationPercent(), profile.initialLockPercent(), profile.trailStepPercent());
 257:                 nextState = rebased.active() ? ProfitLockState.ACTIVE : ProfitLockState.TP_EXTENSION_REBASE;
 258:                 position.setHighestPriceUsdt(rebased.highestPrice());
 259:                 position.setProfitLockProgressPercent(rebased.progressPercent());
 260:                 position.setProfitLockPriceUsdt(rebased.lockPrice());

 535:     private FreshReplayStats generateFreshSignals(
 536:             long runId,
 537:             String symbol,
 538:             Instant executionStart,
 539:             Instant executionEnd,
 540:             List<Candle> oneMinuteCandles,
 541:             List<Candle> fiveMinuteCandles,
 542:             List<Candle> oneHourCandles,
 543:             String btcSymbol,
 544:             List<Candle> btcOneMinuteCandles,
 545:             List<Candle> btcFiveMinuteCandles,
 546:             List<Candle> btcOneHourCandles,
 547:             ReplayDataSource dataSource,
 548:             ReplayDataset replayDataset
 549:     ) {
 550:         List<ReplayCandle> timeline = new java.util.ArrayList<>();
 551:         oneMinuteCandles.forEach(c -> timeline.add(new ReplayCandle(symbol, "1m", c, true)));
 552:         fiveMinuteCandles.forEach(c -> timeline.add(new ReplayCandle(symbol, "5m", c, true)));
 553:         oneHourCandles.forEach(c -> timeline.add(new ReplayCandle(symbol, "1h", c, true)));
 554:         btcOneMinuteCandles.forEach(c -> timeline.add(new ReplayCandle(btcSymbol, "1m", c, false)));
 555:         btcFiveMinuteCandles.forEach(c -> timeline.add(new ReplayCandle(btcSymbol, "5m", c, false)));
 556:         btcOneHourCandles.forEach(c -> timeline.add(new ReplayCandle(btcSymbol, "1h", c, false)));
 557:         timeline.sort(java.util.Comparator
 558:                 .comparing((ReplayCandle rc) -> rc.candle().getOpenTime().plusSeconds(intervalSeconds(rc.interval())))
 559:                 .thenComparingInt(rc -> intervalOrder(rc.interval()))
 560:                 .thenComparingInt(rc -> rc.primary() ? 1 : 0));
 561: 
 562:         int oneMinuteSignals = 0, fiveMinuteSignals = 0, oneHourSignals = 0;
 563:         int oneMinuteBuys = 0, fiveMinuteBuys = 0, oneHourBuys = 0;
 564:         int buys = 0, watches = 0, sells = 0, strongSells = 0, errors = 0;
 565:         java.util.List<TradeSignal> generatedSignals = new java.util.ArrayList<>();
 566: 
 567:         // FIX-11L: Replay-only deep profiling for the Generate fresh signals stage.
 568:         // These monotonic timers observe existing calls only; they do not alter inputs,
 569:         // call ordering, persistence, thresholds, or any Production trading behavior.
 570:         ReplayFreshSignalProfiler profiler = new ReplayFreshSignalProfiler(runId, dataSource);
 571:         // FIX-11M: Enable aggregate timing only for this Replay worker thread.
 572:         // The shared AnalysisService decision path is unchanged; this is observation-only.
 573:         analysisService.beginReplayAnalysisProfiling(runId);
 574:         try (ExecutionReplayScope.Scope ignored = replayScope.open(runId, List.of(), o -> {})) {
 575:         // FIX-043 Replay parity: fresh Replay has always generated technical snapshots/signals
 576:         // chronologically for EVERY closed candle in the timeline. Production now restores the
 577:         // same no-gap contract with asynchronous close-event processing plus chronological recovery.
 578:         // Do not "optimize" Replay by sampling every Nth candle or by copying the production recovery
 579:         // scheduler cadence; that would recreate the exact 1m->~5m blind-gap incident FIX-043 fixes.
 580:         for (int index = 0; index < timeline.size(); index++) {
 581:             checkStopRequested(runId);
 582:             ReplayCandle replay = timeline.get(index);
 583:             Candle candle = replay.candle();
 584:             Instant evaluationTime = candle.getOpenTime().plusSeconds(intervalSeconds(replay.interval()));
 585:             boolean inRequestedWindow = !evaluationTime.isBefore(executionStart) && !evaluationTime.isAfter(executionEnd);
 586:             try {
 587:                 long operationStartedNs = System.nanoTime();
 588:                 java.util.Optional<IndicatorSnapshot> snapshot;
 589:                 try {
 590:                     snapshot = dataSource == ReplayDataSource.DATASET
 591:                             ? technicalIndicatorService.calculateSnapshotForRegression(
 592:                                     replay.symbol(), replay.interval(), candle.getOpenTime(), replayDataset)
 593:                             : technicalIndicatorService.calculateSnapshotForRegression(
 594:                                     replay.symbol(), replay.interval(), candle.getOpenTime());
 595:                 } finally {
 596:                     profiler.recordSnapshot(System.nanoTime() - operationStartedNs);
 597:                 }
 598:                 if (snapshot.isEmpty()) {
 599:                     if (inRequestedWindow) {
 600:                         errors++;
 601:                         saveGenerationError(runId, replay.symbol(), replay.interval(), candle,
 602:                                 "Not enough historical candles to calculate the technical snapshot");
 603:                     }
 604:                     continue;
 605:                 }
 606: 
 607:                 // Do not generate a signal whose candle would only have closed after the
 608:                 // requested test end. Warm-up rows before executionStart are intentionally
 609:                 // generated for as-of context, but are not counted or displayed as test output.

===== src/main/java/com/crypto/execution/service/EntryConsumptionPolicy.java 1-100 =====
   1: package com.crypto.execution.service;
   2: 
   3: import com.crypto.execution.domain.EntryConsumptionState;
   4: import com.crypto.wallet.repository.WalletTradeRepository;
   5: import lombok.RequiredArgsConstructor;
   6: import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
   7: 
   8: /**
   9:  * FIX-112A: consumption belongs to the specific bullish signal, not to the
  10:  * symbol's general position state. A pre-existing position can coexist with a
  11:  * blocked progressive-add signal, so OPEN-position state is not proof that the
  12:  * immediately previous bullish signal actually executed.
  13:  */
  14: @Service
  15: @RequiredArgsConstructor
  16: public class EntryConsumptionPolicy {
  17:     private final WalletTradeRepository walletTradeRepository;
  18:     private final ExecutionReplayScope replayScope;
  19: 
  20:     public EntryConsumptionState resolve(Long previousSignalId) {
  21:         if (previousSignalId == null) return EntryConsumptionState.NOT_CONSUMED;
  22:         if (replayScope.active()) {
  23:             return replayScope.entryConsumed(previousSignalId)
  24:                     ? EntryConsumptionState.CONSUMED
  25:                     : EntryConsumptionState.NOT_CONSUMED;
  26:         }
  27:         // Production authority is the immutable executed BUY row keyed to the
  28:         // exact triggering signal. This works for both first entries and adds.
  29:         boolean executed = walletTradeRepository
  30:                 .findTopBySignalIdAndSideAndStatusOrderByExecutedAtDesc(
  31:                         previousSignalId, "BUY", "EXECUTED")
  32:                 .isPresent();
  33:         return executed ? EntryConsumptionState.CONSUMED : EntryConsumptionState.NOT_CONSUMED;
  34:     }
  35: }

 478:                 List<Candle> forward = candleRepository
 479:                         .findBySymbolAndIntervalCodeAndClosedTrueAndOpenTimeBetweenOrderByOpenTimeAsc(
 480:                                 sym, interval, start, end);
 481:                 List<Candle> merged = new java.util.ArrayList<>(prefix.size() + forward.size());
 482:                 merged.addAll(prefix);
 483:                 Instant prefixEnd = prefix.isEmpty() ? Instant.EPOCH : prefix.get(prefix.size() - 1).getOpenTime();
 484:                 forward.stream().filter(c -> c.getOpenTime().isAfter(prefixEnd)).forEach(merged::add);
 485:                 candleMap.put(new ReplayDataset.CandleKey(sym, interval), merged);
 486:                 log.info("FIX-11H dataset candles: symbol={}, interval={}, prefix={}, forward={}, merged={}",
 487:                         sym, interval, prefix.size(), forward.size(), merged.size());
 488:             }
 489:         }
 490: 
 491:         Map<ReplayDataset.SignalKey, Long> lineage = new HashMap<>();
 492:         // FIX-11H / FIX-112D: lineage is candle identity, not signal persistence timing.
 493:         // Recovery/backfilled Production signals can be generated hours after their candle, so
 494:         // generatedAt MUST NOT define this preload window. Select and match lineage by the same
 495:         // exact candleOpenTime identity used by ReplayDataset.sourceSignalId().
 496:         for (TradeSignal signal : signalRepository.findBySymbolAndCandleOpenTimeBetweenOrderByCandleOpenTimeAsc(symbol, start, end)) {
 497:             ReplayDataset.SignalKey key = new ReplayDataset.SignalKey(
 498:                     signal.getSymbol(), signal.getInterval(), signal.getCandleOpenTime());
 499:             Long previous = lineage.putIfAbsent(key, signal.getId());
 500:             if (previous != null && !previous.equals(signal.getId())) {
 501:                 throw new IllegalStateException("Replay lineage invariant violated for " + key
 502:                         + ": signalIds=" + previous + "," + signal.getId());
 503:             }
 504:         }
 505:         log.info("FIX-11H dataset lineage: symbol={}, entries={}", symbol, lineage.size());
 506:         return new ReplayDataset(candleMap, lineage);
 507:     }

 514:     private int verifyEventResolution(long runId, String symbol, String interval, List<Candle> candles,
 515:                                       int progressStart, int progressEnd) {
 516:         int resolved = 0;
 517:         int size = candles.size();
 518:         for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
 519:             checkStopRequested(runId);
 520:             Candle candle = candles.get(i);
 521:             List<Candle> latestAtEvent = candleRepository.findClosedCandlesAtOrBefore(
 522:                     symbol, interval, candle.getOpenTime(), PageRequest.of(0, 1));
 523:             if (!latestAtEvent.isEmpty() && candle.getOpenTime().equals(latestAtEvent.get(0).getOpenTime())) {
 524:                 resolved++;
 525:             }
 526:             if (i % 25 == 0 && size > 0) {
 527:                 int p = progressStart + (int) Math.round((progressEnd - progressStart) * (i / (double) size));
 528:                 updateRun(runId, "RUNNING", p,
 529:                         "Replaying " + interval + " candle " + (i + 1) + "/" + size, null);
 530:             }
 531:         }
 532:         return resolved;
 533:     }
