agent-docs\runs\20261011-224337\round01-codex.stderr.txt:72:**Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. The recorded entries therefore reach Replay only as an **immutable entry-fixture dataset**, prepared by a separate read-only extraction that runs outside the Replay execution boundary and is never part of a Replay run. Each fixture holds: symbol, position identifier, recorded entry time, execution price and the observed-at time of that price, the entry signal identifier, the normalised fixed-notional basis (the recorded quantity is kept for audit and is not used for sizing), initial stop loss and take profit, entry scores, entry-consumption state, and the protection state at entry. The dataset has a content hash recorded in the run certificate. Replay reads the fixture file or Replay-owned fixture table only; the forbidden-dependency guard still applies to every account table. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

agent-docs\runs\20261011-224337\round01-codex.stderr.txt:262:The FIX-156 outcome target is **at least 99% agreement among qualified, comparable decisions, measured separately for signal parity and for lifecycle parity (Section 7.1); the two are never pooled**. A unit is one Production-recorded signal decision or position outcome. It passes only when the versioned comparison agrees on entry versus no entry, exit versus hold, exit reason, exit timestamp, and exit price within the frozen tolerance. Wallet-driven cases, insufficient-evidence cases and refused cases are excluded from the denominator and reported separately; none may be counted as a match. Every disagreement has a one-line classified cause. Average P&L is not a substitute for this decision-level metric.
agent-docs\runs\20261011-224337\round01-codex.stderr.txt:264:**Validity conditions (frozen before the first measured run):** (a) a minimum coverage, meaning comparable cases as a share of all Production decisions in the window, reported next to the agreement rate; (b) a minimum number of comparable cases; (c) a lower confidence bound on the agreement rate, and the 99% target is judged on that bound, not the raw percentage; (d) the numeric values are set by the team from E06 evidence and approved by the owner. A result that fails (a) or (b) is reported as **not evaluable**, never as a pass.

agent-docs\runs\20261011-224337\round01-codex.stderr.txt:1877:**Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. The recorded entries therefore reach Replay only as an **immutable entry-fixture dataset**, prepared by a separate read-only extraction that runs outside the Replay execution boundary and is never part of a Replay run. Each fixture holds: symbol, position identifier, recorded entry time, execution price and the observed-at time of that price, the entry signal identifier, the normalised fixed-notional basis (the recorded quantity is kept for audit and is not used for sizing), initial stop loss and take profit, entry scores, entry-consumption state, and the protection state at entry. The dataset has a content hash recorded in the run certificate. Replay reads the fixture file or Replay-owned fixture table only; the forbidden-dependency guard still applies to every account table. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

agent-docs\runs\20261011-224337\round01-codex.stderr.txt:2067:The FIX-156 outcome target is **at least 99% agreement among qualified, comparable decisions, measured separately for signal parity and for lifecycle parity (Section 7.1); the two are never pooled**. A unit is one Production-recorded signal decision or position outcome. It passes only when the versioned comparison agrees on entry versus no entry, exit versus hold, exit reason, exit timestamp, and exit price within the frozen tolerance. Wallet-driven cases, insufficient-evidence cases and refused cases are excluded from the denominator and reported separately; none may be counted as a match. Every disagreement has a one-line classified cause. Average P&L is not a substitute for this decision-level metric.
agent-docs\runs\20261011-224337\round01-codex.stderr.txt:2069:**Validity conditions (frozen before the first measured run):** (a) a minimum coverage, meaning comparable cases as a share of all Production decisions in the window, reported next to the agreement rate; (b) a minimum number of comparable cases; (c) a lower confidence bound on the agreement rate, and the 99% target is judged on that bound, not the raw percentage; (d) the numeric values are set by the team from E06 evidence and approved by the owner. A result that fails (a) or (b) is reported as **not evaluable**, never as a pass.

agent-docs\runs\20261011-224337\round01-codex.stderr.txt:3119:**Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

agent-docs\runs\20261011-224337\round01-codex.prompt.txt:250:The FIX-156 outcome target is **at least 99% agreement among qualified, comparable decisions, measured separately for signal parity and for lifecycle parity (Section 7.1); the two are never pooled**. agent-docs\runs\20261011-230204\round01-codex.stderr.txt:262:The FIX-156 outcome target is **at least 99% agreement among qualified, comparable decisions, measured separately for signal parity and for lifecycle parity (Section 7.1); the two are never pooled**. A unit is one Production-recorded signal decision or position outcome. It passes only when the versioned comparison agrees on entry versus no entry, exit versus hold, exit reason, exit timestamp, and exit price within the frozen tolerance. Wallet-driven cases, insufficient-evidence cases and refused cases are excluded from the denominator and reported separately; none may be counted as a match. Every disagreement has a one-line classified cause. Average P&L is not a substitute for this decision-level metric.
agent-docs\runs\20261011-230204\round01-codex.stderr.txt:264:**Validity conditions (frozen before the first measured run):** (a) a minimum coverage, meaning comparable cases as a share of all Production decisions in the window, reported next to the agreement rate; (b) a minimum number of comparable cases; (c) a lower confidence bound on the agreement rate, and the 99% target is judged on that bound, not the raw percentage; (d) the numeric values are set by the team from E06 evidence and approved by the owner. A result that fails (a) or (b) is reported as **not evaluable**, never as a pass.

agent-docs\runs\20261011-230204\round01-codex.stderr.txt:2798:**Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. The recorded entries therefore reach Replay only as an **immutable entry-fixture dataset**, prepared by a separate read-only extraction that runs outside the Replay execution boundary and is never part of a Replay run. Each fixture holds: symbol, position identifier, recorded entry time, execution price and the observed-at time of that price, the entry signal identifier, the normalised fixed-notional basis (the recorded quantity is kept for audit and is not used for sizing), initial stop loss and take profit, entry scores, entry-consumption state, and the protection state at entry. The dataset has a content hash recorded in the run certificate. Replay reads the fixture file or Replay-owned fixture table only; the forbidden-dependency guard still applies to every account table. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

agent-docs\runs\20261011-230204\round01-codex.stderr.txt:2992:The FIX-156 outcome target is **at least 99% agreement among qualified, comparable decisions, measured separately for signal parity and for lifecycle parity (Section 7.1); the two are never pooled**. A unit is one Production-recorded signal decision or position outcome. It passes only when the versioned comparison agrees on entry versus no entry, exit versus hold, exit reason, exit timestamp, and exit price within the frozen tolerance. Wallet-driven cases, insufficient-evidence cases and refused cases are excluded from the denominator and reported separately; none may be counted as a match. Every disagreement has a one-line classified cause. Average P&L is not a substitute for this decision-level metric.
agent-docs\runs\20261011-230204\round01-codex.stderr.txt:2994:**Validity conditions (frozen before the first measured run):** (a) a minimum coverage, meaning comparable cases as a share of all Production decisions in the window, reported next to the agreement rate; (b) a minimum number of comparable cases; (c) a lower confidence bound on the agreement rate, and the 99% target is judged on that bound, not the raw percentage; (d) the numeric values are set by the team from E06 evidence and approved by the owner. A result that fails (a) or (b) is reported as **not evaluable**, never as a pass.

agent-docs\runs\20261011-230204\round01-codex.stderr.txt:3243:The FIX-156 outcome target is **at least 99% agreement among qualified, comparable decisions, measured separately for signal parity and for lifecycle parity (Section 7.1); the two are never pooled**. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

agent-docs\runs\20261011-224337\handoff\ORIGINAL_CONTEXT.md:36:**Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. The recorded entries therefore reach Replay only as an **immutable entry-fixture dataset**, prepared by a separate read-only extraction that runs outside the Replay execution boundary and is never part of a Replay run. Each fixture holds: symbol, position identifier, recorded entry time, execution price and the observed-at time of that price, the entry signal identifier, the normalised fixed-notional basis (the recorded quantity is kept for audit and is not used for sizing), initial stop loss and take profit, entry scores, entry-consumption state, and the protection state at entry. The dataset has a content hash recorded in the run certificate. Replay reads the fixture file or Replay-owned fixture table only; the forbidden-dependency guard still applies to every account table. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

agent-docs\runs\20261011-224337\handoff\ORIGINAL_CONTEXT.md:226:The FIX-156 outcome target is **at least 99% agreement among qualified, comparable decisions, measured separately for signal parity and for lifecycle parity (Section 7.1); the two are never pooled**. A unit is one Production-recorded signal decision or position outcome. It passes only when the versioned comparison agrees on entry versus no entry, exit versus hold, exit reason, exit timestamp, and exit price within the frozen tolerance. Wallet-driven cases, insufficient-evidence cases and refused cases are excluded from the denominator and reported separately; none may be counted as a match. Every disagreement has a one-line classified cause. Average P&L is not a substitute for this decision-level metric.
agent-docs\runs\20261011-224337\handoff\ORIGINAL_CONTEXT.md:228:**Validity conditions (frozen before the first measured run):** (a) a minimum coverage, meaning comparable cases as a share of all Production decisions in the window, reported next to the agreement rate; (b) a minimum number of comparable cases; (c) a lower confidence bound on the agreement rate, and the 99% target is judged on that bound, not the raw percentage; (d) the numeric values are set by the team from E06 evidence and approved by the owner. A result that fails (a) or (b) is reported as **not evaluable**, never as a pass.

agent-docs\runs\20261011-230204\handoff\ORIGINAL_CONTEXT.md:36:**Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. Each fixture holds: symbol, position identifier, recorded entry time, execution price and the observed-at time of that price, the entry signal identifier, the normalised fixed-notional basis (the recorded quantity is kept for audit and is not used for sizing), initial stop loss and take profit, entry scores, entry-consumption state, and the protection state at entry. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

agent-docs\runs\20261011-230204\handoff\ORIGINAL_CONTEXT.md:226:The FIX-156 outcome target is **at least 99% agreement among qualified, comparable decisions, measured separately for signal parity and for lifecycle parity (Section 7.1); the two are never pooled**. A unit is one Production-recorded signal decision or position outcome. It passes only when the versioned comparison agrees on entry versus no entry, exit versus hold, exit reason, exit timestamp, and exit price within the frozen tolerance. Wallet-driven cases, insufficient-evidence cases and refused cases are excluded from the denominator and reported separately; none may be counted as a match. Every disagreement has a one-line classified cause. Average P&L is not a substitute for this decision-level metric.
agent-docs\runs\20261011-230204\handoff\ORIGINAL_CONTEXT.md:228:**Validity conditions (frozen before the first measured run):** (a) a minimum coverage, meaning comparable cases as a share of all Production decisions in the window, reported next to the agreement rate; (b) a minimum number of comparable cases; (c) a lower confidence bound on the agreement rate, and the 99% target is judged on that bound, not the raw percentage; (d) the numeric values are set by the team from E06 evidence and approved by the owner. A result that fails (a) or (b) is reported as **not evaluable**, never as a pass.

agent-docs\runs\20261011-023447\handoff\ORIGINAL_CONTEXT.md:226:The FIX-156 outcome target is **at least 99% agreement among qualified, comparable decisions, measured separately for signal parity and for lifecycle parity (Section 7.1); the two are never pooled**. A unit is one Production-recorded signal decision or position outcome. It passes only when the versioned comparison agrees on entry versus no entry, exit versus hold, exit reason, exit timestamp, and exit price within the frozen tolerance. Wallet-driven cases, insufficient-evidence cases and refused cases are excluded from the denominator and reported separately; none may be counted as a match. Every disagreement has a one-line classified cause. Average P&L is not a substitute for this decision-level metric.
agent-docs\runs\20261011-023447\handoff\ORIGINAL_CONTEXT.md:228:**Validity conditions (frozen before the first measured run):** (a) a minimum coverage, meaning comparable cases as a share of all Production decisions in the window, reported next to the agreement rate; (b) a minimum number of comparable cases; (c) a lower confidence bound on the agreement rate, and the 99% target is judged on that bound, not the raw percentage; (d) the numeric values are set by the team from E06 evidence and approved by the owner. A result that fails (a) or (b) is reported as **not evaluable**, never as a pass.

agent-docs\runs\20261011-023447\round01-codex.prompt.txt:250:The FIX-156 outcome target is **at least 99% agreement among qualified, comparable decisions, measured separately for signal parity and for lifecycle parity (Section 7.1); the two are never pooled**. A unit is one Production-recorded signal decision or position outcome. It passes only when the versioned comparison agrees on entry versus no entry, exit versus hold, exit reason, exit timestamp, and exit price within the frozen tolerance. Wallet-driven cases, insufficient-evidence cases and refused cases are excluded from the denominator and reported separately; none may be counted as a match. Every disagreement has a one-line classified cause. Average P&L is not a substitute for this decision-level metric.
agent-docs\runs\20261011-023447\round01-codex.prompt.txt:252:**Validity conditions (frozen before the first measured run):** (a) a minimum coverage, meaning comparable cases as a share of all Production decisions in the window, reported next to the agreement rate; (b) a minimum number of comparable cases; (c) a lower confidence bound on the agreement rate, and the 99% target is judged on that bound, not the raw percentage; (d) the numeric values are set by the team from E06 evidence and approved by the owner. A result that fails (a) or (b) is reported as **not evaluable**, never as a pass.

agent-docs\runs\20261011-023447\round01-codex.stderr.txt:72:**Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. The dataset has a content hash recorded in the run certificate. Replay reads the fixture file or Replay-owned fixture table only; the forbidden-dependency guard still applies to every account table. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

agent-docs\runs\20261011-023447\round01-codex.stderr.txt:262:The FIX-156 outcome target is **at least 99% agreement among qualified, comparable decisions, measured separately for signal parity and for lifecycle parity (Section 7.1); the two are never pooled**. A unit is one Production-recorded signal decision or position outcome. It passes only when the versioned comparison agrees on entry versus no entry, exit versus hold, exit reason, exit timestamp, and exit price within the frozen tolerance. Wallet-driven cases, insufficient-evidence cases and refused cases are excluded from the denominator and reported separately; none may be counted as a match. Every disagreement has a one-line classified cause. Average P&L is not a substitute for this decision-level metric.
agent-docs\runs\20261011-023447\round01-codex.stderr.txt:264:**Validity conditions (frozen before the first measured run):** (a) a minimum coverage, meaning comparable cases as a share of all Production decisions in the window, reported next to the agreement rate; (b) a minimum number of comparable cases; (c) a lower confidence bound on the agreement rate, and the 99% target is judged on that bound, not the raw percentage; (d) the numeric values are set by the team from E06 evidence and approved by the owner. A result that fails (a) or (b) is reported as **not evaluable**, never as a pass.

agent-docs\runs\20261011-023447\round01-codex.stderr.txt:1868:**Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. The recorded entries therefore reach Replay only as an **immutable entry-fixture dataset**, prepared by a separate read-only extraction that runs outside the Replay execution boundary and is never part of a Replay run. Each fixture holds: symbol, position identifier, recorded entry time, execution price and the observed-at time of that price, the entry signal identifier, the normalised fixed-notional basis (the recorded quantity is kept for audit and is not used for sizing), initial stop loss and take profit, entry scores, entry-consumption state, and the protection state at entry. The dataset has a content hash recorded in the run certificate. Replay reads the fixture file or Replay-owned fixture table only; the forbidden-dependency guard still applies to every account table. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

agent-docs\runs\20261011-023447\round01-codex.stderr.txt:3613:  36: **Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. ===== src/main/java/com/crypto/service/BuyHtfAssessmentAuditStore.java 20-90 =====
  20:  * connection inside an execution transaction and never changes a BUY result.
  21:  */
  22: @Slf4j
  23: @Component
  24: public class BuyHtfAssessmentAuditStore {
  25:     private final JdbcTemplate jdbc;
  26:     private final Executor executor;
  27:     private final Fix154Metrics metrics;
  28:     @Autowired(required = false)
  29:     private ExecutionReplayScope replayScope;
  30: 
  31:     public BuyHtfAssessmentAuditStore(JdbcTemplate jdbc, @Qualifier("fix154AuditExecutor") Executor executor,
  32:                                       Fix154Metrics metrics) {
  33:         this.jdbc = jdbc;
  34:         this.executor = executor;
  35:         this.metrics = metrics;
  36:     }
  37: 
  38:     public void record(TradeSignal reference, String path,
  39:                        HigherTimeframeBuyAssessmentService.Assessment assessment,
  40:                        String finalResult, String reason) {
  41:         // Replay signals are JDBC-generated and have no entity id. Replay parity
  42:         // uses its own evidence tables; never write a misleading Production audit.
  43:         if (reference == null || assessment == null || reference.getId() == null
  44:                 || (replayScope != null && replayScope.active())) return;
  45:         AuditPayload payload = AuditPayload.from(reference, path, assessment, finalResult, reason);
  46:         try {
  47:             executor.execute(() -> persist(payload));
  48:         } catch (RejectedExecutionException rejected) {
  49:             metrics.auditWriteFailed();
  50:             log.warn("FIX-154 assessment audit queue is full; BUY decision remains unchanged: path={}, referenceSignalId={}",
  51:                     path, reference.getId());
  52:         }
  53:     }
  54: 
  55:     private void persist(AuditPayload p) {
  56:         try {
  57:             jdbc.update("""
  58:                     INSERT INTO buy_htf_assessment_audit (
  59:                       reference_signal_id, evaluation_path, evaluated_at, replay_mode,
  60:                       one_hour_signal_id, one_hour_raw_decision, one_hour_effective_decision,
  61:                       one_hour_candle_close_time, one_hour_age_seconds, one_hour_data_quality_valid, one_hour_usability_reason,
  62:                       five_minute_signal_id, five_minute_raw_decision, five_minute_effective_decision,
  63:                       five_minute_candle_close_time, five_minute_age_seconds, five_minute_data_quality_valid, five_minute_usability_reason,
  64:                       confidence_threshold, assessment_band, hard_confirmation_present, max_initial_percent,
  65:                       legacy_veto_result, final_result, final_reason)
  66:                     VALUES (?, ?, ?, FALSE, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
  67:                     """,
  68:                     p.referenceId, p.path, Timestamp.from(p.evaluatedAt),
  69:                     p.one.id, p.one.decision, p.effectiveOne, timestamp(p.one.candleClose), p.one.ageSeconds, p.one.quality, p.one.usability,
  70:                     p.five.id, p.five.decision, p.effectiveFive, timestamp(p.five.candleClose), p.five.ageSeconds, p.five.quality, p.five.usability,
  71:                     HigherTimeframeBuyAssessmentService.HARD_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD, p.band, p.hardConfirmationPresent, p.maxInitialPercent,
  72:                     p.legacyVeto, p.finalResult, p.reason);
  73:         } catch (Exception e) {
  74:             metrics.auditWriteFailed();
  75:             log.warn("FIX-154 assessment audit was not recorded; BUY decision remains unchanged: path={}, referenceSignalId={}",
  76:                     p.path, p.referenceId, e);
  77:         }
  78:     }
  79: 
  80:     private static Timestamp timestamp(Instant value) { return value == null ? null : Timestamp.from(value); }
  81: 
  82:     private record Context(Long id, String decision, Instant candleClose, Long ageSeconds, Boolean quality, String usability) {
  83:         static Context from(TradeSignal signal, Instant evaluatedAt) {
  84:             if (signal == null) return new Context(null, null, null, null, null, "MISSING");
  85:             Instant close = deriveCandleClose(signal);
  86:             Long age = close == null ? null : Math.max(0L, Duration.between(close, evaluatedAt).getSeconds());
  87:             return new Context(signal.getId(), signal.getDecision() == null ? null : signal.getDecision().name(), close, age,
  88:                     signal.getDataQualityValid(), Boolean.TRUE.equals(signal.getDataQualityValid()) ? "AVAILABLE" : "QUALITY_UNKNOWN");
  89:         }
  90:     }

  17:  * and restored in finally; open-position additions never enter this scope. Replay uses
  18:  * its own executed stops, never Production history. No wallet lock or balance writes.

  20: @Service

  22: public class StopLossEvidenceService {

  24:     private final ExecutionReplayScope replay;

  29: 
  30:     @Autowired
  31:     public StopLossEvidenceService(StopLossEvidenceStore store, ExecutionReplayScope replay,
  32:                                   ObjectMapper mapper, @Value("${trading.fix122.enabled:true}") boolean enabled) {
  33:         this(store,replay,mapper,enabled,Clock.systemUTC());
  34:     }
  35: 
  36:     StopLossEvidenceService(StopLossEvidenceStore store, ExecutionReplayScope replay,
  37:                            ObjectMapper mapper, boolean enabled, Clock clock) {
  38:         this.store=store; this.replay=replay; this.mapper=mapper; this.enabled=enabled; this.clock=clock;
  39:     }
  40: 
  41:     private boolean enabled() { return replay.active() ? replay.fix122Enabled() : enabled; }
  42:     private Instant now() { return replay.active() ? replay.referenceInstant() : clock.instant(); }
  43:     private StopLossEvidencePolicy.Boundary resolve(String symbol, Instant at) {
  44:         return replay.active() ? replay.stopBoundary(symbol, at) : store.latest(symbol, at);
  45:     }
  46:     public boolean hasBoundary() { return active.get()!=null && active.get().boundary!=null; }
  47: 
  48:     public ExecutionDecision evaluate(TradeSignal signal, int allocation, Supplier<ExecutionDecision> action) {
  49:         if (allocation>0 || signal==null || signal.getGeneratedAt()==null || !enabled()) return action.get();
  50:         return scoped(signal, () -> new SetupWakeupEvaluation(signal, action.get())).decision();
  51:     }

  58:     private SetupWakeupEvaluation scoped(TradeSignal trigger, Supplier<SetupWakeupEvaluation> action) {
  59:         Context previous=active.get();
  60:         Context c=new Context(trigger, now(), replay.active()?replay.runId():null);
  61:         active.set(c);
  62:         try {
  63:             try { c.boundary=resolve(trigger.getSymbol(), c.at); }
  64:             catch (RuntimeException error) {
  65:                 log.warn("[FIX-122] BOUNDARY_UNAVAILABLE symbol={} signalId={}", trigger.getSymbol(), trigger.getId(), error);
  66:                 c.status="BOUNDARY_UNAVAILABLE";
  67:                 ExecutionDecision d=ExecutionDecision.reject("FIX122_BOUNDARY_UNAVAILABLE",
  68:                         "Stop history could not be checked. Entry deferred to the next normal evaluation.");
  69:                 audit(c,d,"EVALUATION");
  70:                 return new SetupWakeupEvaluation(trigger,d);
  71:             }

  73:             if ("1m".equals(trigger.getInterval()) && !eligible(trigger,"CURRENT_SIGNAL")) {
  74:                 result=new SetupWakeupEvaluation(trigger, ExecutionDecision.reject("FIX122_CURRENT_CANDLE_STALE",
  75:                         "Current entry candle is not eligible after the completed stop-loss."));
  76:             } else {
  77:                 try { result=action.get(); }
  78:                 catch (StaleCurrent ignored) {
  79:                     result=new SetupWakeupEvaluation(c.current,ExecutionDecision.reject("FIX122_CURRENT_CANDLE_STALE",
  80:                             "Wake-up timing candle is not eligible after the completed stop-loss."));
  81:                 }
  82:             }
  83:             if (result!=null && result.decision()!=null) {
  84:                 result=new SetupWakeupEvaluation(result.executionSignal(), result.decision()
  85:                         .withStopBoundary(new StopLossEvidencePolicy.Stamp(c.boundary)));
  86:             }
  87:             audit(c,result==null?null:result.decision(),"EVALUATION");
  88:             return result==null?SetupWakeupEvaluation.none():result;
  89:         } finally {
  90:             if(previous==null) active.remove(); else active.set(previous);
  91:         }
  92:     }

  94:     public void requireCurrent(TradeSignal signal) {
  95:         if(active.get()!=null) active.get().current=signal;
  96:         if(!eligible(signal,"CURRENT_SIGNAL")) throw new StaleCurrent();
  97:     }

  99:     public boolean eligible(TradeSignal signal, String purpose) {
 100:         Context c=active.get();
 101:         if(c==null || c.boundary==null) return true;
 102:         String reason=signal==null?"LINEAGE_UNRESOLVED":StopLossEvidencePolicy.exclusion(
 103:                 signal.getInterval(),signal.getCandleOpenTime(),signal.getGeneratedAt(),c.at,c.boundary);
 104:         if(reason==null) return true;
 105:         Map<String,Object> item=new LinkedHashMap<>();
 106:         item.put("purpose",purpose); item.put("reason",reason);
 107:         if(signal!=null) {
 108:             item.put("signalId",signal.getId()); item.put("interval",signal.getInterval());
 109:             item.put("candleOpenTime",String.valueOf(signal.getCandleOpenTime()));
 110:             item.put("decision",String.valueOf(signal.getDecision()));
 111:         }
 112:         if(!c.excluded.contains(item)) c.excluded.add(item);
 113:         return false;
 114:     }

  13: /**
  14:  * FIX-056 fresh execution-price authority.
  15:  *
  16:  * <p>TradeSignal.latestPrice is immutable decision-time evidence and must never be
  17:  * treated as an execution fill. Production resolves the newest canonical Binance 1m
  18:  * live-price event recorded by FIX-052. Administration Replay resolves the newest
  19:  * replay price event already consumed by ExecutionReplayScope. This gives both paths
  20:  * one price authority while preserving the original signal snapshot for audit.</p>
  21:  */
  22: @Service
  23: @RequiredArgsConstructor
  24: public class ExecutionPriceAuthorityService {
  25:     private static final Duration MAX_EXECUTION_PRICE_AGE = Duration.ofSeconds(15);
  26: 
  27:     private final MarketPriceEventService marketPriceEventService;
  28:     private final ExecutionReplayScope replayScope;
  29: 
  30:     public Optional<ExecutionPrice> resolve(String symbol, Instant referenceTime) {
  31:         // FIX-109 / Replay parity: wall-clock fallback is forbidden. Every caller must
  32:         // supply the evaluation clock explicitly so historical Replay can never silently
  33:         // compare an old market event with the machine clock used by Production today.
  34:         Instant reference = Objects.requireNonNull(referenceTime,
  35:                 "Execution price reference time is required");
  36: 
  37:         if (replayScope.active()) {
  38:             return replayScope.latestPrice()
  39:                     .filter(p -> symbol != null && symbol.equalsIgnoreCase(p.symbol()))
  40:                     .filter(p -> !p.observedAt().isAfter(reference))
  41:                     .filter(p -> !Duration.between(p.observedAt(), reference).isNegative())
  42:                     .filter(p -> Duration.between(p.observedAt(), reference).compareTo(MAX_EXECUTION_PRICE_AGE) <= 0)
  43:                     .map(p -> new ExecutionPrice(p.price(), p.observedAt(), "REPLAY_MARKET_PRICE_EVENT"));
  44:         }
  45: 
  46:         return marketPriceEventService.findLatestAtOrBefore(symbol, reference)
  47:                 .filter(p -> Duration.between(p.observedAt(), reference).compareTo(MAX_EXECUTION_PRICE_AGE) <= 0)
  48:                 .map(p -> new ExecutionPrice(p.price(), p.observedAt(), p.source()));
  49:     }
  50: 
  51:     public record ExecutionPrice(BigDecimal price, Instant observedAt, String source) {}
  52: }

## FINDINGS

- **PROJECT EVIDENCE:** The preparation is explicitly incomplete: P01–P07 are all pending, E03–E10 are absent, and the canonical specification is still RPR-0.4 draft—not the stated RPR-0.9.11 revision. The RPR-0.9.11 source file is not present in the workspace.

- **PROJECT EVIDENCE:** E01 correctly identifies major current violations: Replay reads `wallet_settings`, calls shared BUY validation, can call Binance `exchangeInfo`, writes `fix122_evaluation`, and uses wallet-shaped replay tables/state.

- **PROJECT EVIDENCE:** The proposed historical fixture scope is materially incomplete for analysis parity. Current `analyzeForRegression` consumes sentiment, fundamentals, prior indicators, market context, strategy configuration, BTC context, historical order-book data, derivatives configuration, ATR/data-quality rules, and scoring configuration. The preparation names a BUY policy profile and sentiment fixture, but does not yet require a complete dated analysis-policy/configuration snapshot or a refusal classification for every missing input.

- **PROJECT EVIDENCE:** The preparation’s endpoint boundary is underspecified. It names `/runs/**`, yet the same Replay controller exposes `/proven-trades`; its enrichment can read `wallet_trade`. That route must be explicitly excluded, redesigned, or brought inside the enforced boundary.

- **PROJECT EVIDENCE:** The current replay signal timeline uses generated time, while FIX-156 correctly proposes E07-derived availability time. E07 remains pending, so same-boundary ordering is not implementable yet.

- **AGENT INFERENCE:** “Replay only; no Production source changes” conflicts with registry items naming shared production-used classes (`ExecutionReplayScope`, `MarketPriceEventService`). The frozen contract must either define strictly Replay-owned adapters or clarify the permitted shared-source edits and prove zero Production behavioural impact.

## OBJECTIONS

- **AGENT INFERENCE:** Do not freeze an acceptance metric before E03/E06 establishes coverage, exclusions, comparable count, lower-confidence-bound method, and the sealed acceptance cohort. Otherwise a high result can be produced by excluding difficult or unavailable cases.

- **AGENT INFERENCE:** A static “table-name/repository/HTTP-client” test is useful but insufficiently specified as the sole guard. The contract needs an exact Replay reachability graph, explicit allow-list ownership, and test cases for reflective/dynamic SQL and asynchronous scope loss.

- **AGENT INFERENCE:** The required Replay executor has no exact bean/configuration ownership yet. Current `RegressionTestWorker.runAsync` uses unqualified `@Async`; the future contract must name the executor, queue, rejection behaviour, scope propagation mechanism, and numerical capacity limits.
